datasheet.title: Eaton ePDU G3 specification drawing for EMIT03-10 (EMI3MGB5EMB13A1), revision 002

description: Eaton ePDU G3 metered input rack PDU, 1U horizontal, 120 V. A 19 in black metal box, 203.2 mm deep, that takes a single-phase 120 V feed (a fixed 10 ft cord ending in a NEMA L5-30P, 24 A) and hands it on to 12 NEMA 5-20R outlets in two colour-coded sections of six, each on its own 20 A one-pole breaker, A (yellow) and B (blue). The controls end carries the hot-swappable meter module (two RJ-45 ports (serial and daisy-chain), a network RJ-45, a USB-A port, a pixel display and four buttons), the two breakers and outlets A1 and A2; the other end carries the cord gland and the remaining ten outlets. The meter reads the input and each section.

gaps.note: no photograph of this model is held. The sheet says "BLACK CHASSIS" and its section outlines are yellow and blue; the brochure's page 3 photographs of 1U G3+ units (a later generation than the 2015 sheet) show a black chassis and module, yellow (A) and blue (B) lettered tiles, light blue buttons with white symbols and a lit blue-violet screen. The buttons' light blue and the tiles' two hues are taken from them and are borrowed, not measured on this model. The chassis hex, the unlit display's dark blue and the breaker handles are stand-ins.

the sheet draws a round 12.9 point at the left end of the controls face with the earth symbol under it, and names no part. It is placed as a ground screw on a washer (common/ground-screw-washer@1, 11.0), the library's part of that kind; the size and the kind of fixing are not stated.

gaps.note: the meter is hot-swappable but no held document draws it apart from the faceplate, so no bay and no module component stand for it; the ports, display and buttons are placed on the face.

gaps.note: the sheet draws a plate with a lever, two crosses, a triangle and a ring above each IEC outlet of the EMIT04-10; the EMIT03-10's NEMA outlets draw none. Nothing is drawn here.
the plan shows two bands 16.7 and 17.2 deep along the rear and front edges and six screws, and no figure gives their relief. Only the screws are drawn.

the quick start (P-164000314_2, July 2014, page 2) names a serial or EMP port, an Ethernet port, a USB port, a reset button and a daisy chain port for the module, and its drawing is too small to tell which of the sheet's stacked pair of RJ-45 sockets is the serial port and which the daisy chain. The upper is drawn as the serial port and the lower, under the chain symbol, as the daisy chain; the order is an assumption. The quick start allows four units on a chain where the product overview (PA155003EN, 2018) says eight.

name: emit03-10

breakers.note: drawing - "CIRCUIT BREAKERS (2) 20A 1-POLE UL LISTED": one breaker per section, each in the live line only (the one-line diagram: L through the meter and breaker to the section, N straight through).

capability.note: drawing - FUNCTIONALITY "CURRENT, POWER AND ENERGY METERING FOR INPUT & BRANCH"; the overview lists "Phase and section metering" and no outlet-level or switching feature for the Metered Input tier. So `metering-scope: branch` (the section is the finest level) and `outlet-switching: false`.

chassis.note: drawing - 42.9 high, 203.2 deep, 482.6 over the ears; the body reads 444.4 to 444.6 between the ears' inner edges, so it is 444.5 and each ear 19.05 (three quarters of an inch). "BLACK CHASSIS" (the sheet's MECHANICAL cell); the hex #1f2022 is a stand-in, as the other Eaton strips'. The brochure (BR155022EN, page 3) shows black metal. The Eaton Rack PDU G3 product overview (PA155003EN) lists "Low-weight aluminum chassis". No weight is stated by any held document (gaps: weight).

dcim.note: the input is one power port (eaton/g3-cord-l5-30p@1) and each outlet a `nema-5-20r` power outlet fed by it, named as printed, A1 to A6 and B1 to B6. No `feed_leg` is written: a single-phase PDU is on whatever leg its plug is on.

ears.note: drawing - the sheet draws a rack ear at each end of the controls face, an L flange 19.05 wide with a slot, and the plan shows the flange at the controls end only. The library's generic ear stands for them (`chassis.ears`). The overview says "Flexible mounting options allows you to choose your preferred mounting method between 0U or 1U/2U" and the brochure "Horizontal units (1U/2U) come with rack ear support"; the position is flush, as drawn.

front.note: drawing - mm from the body's left and top, as seen from the front. The meter module's plate from 21.9 to 166.7 across and 1.7 to 39.5 down; two RJ-45 ports (serial above, daisy-chain below) centred 33.6 across and 10.9 and 27.4 down; the network RJ-45 centred (57.2, 13.4) and the USB-A under it (57.2, 25.1); the reset button ("R" and a ring) at (70.9, 24.9); four buttons 12.0 by 11.8, up and down at 96.8 across (8.8 and 32.6 down) and ESC and enter at 153.8; the pixel display 30.4 by 33.6 at (110.2, 4.2); the Eaton wordmark from 77.1 to 96.3 across and 16.7 to 23.6 down (not drawn). Beyond the module: breaker A's plate at 179.1 across and 10.4 down, breaker B's at 241.3, each 59.2 by 19.5; outlets A1 and A2 centred 373.3 and 411.9 across and 21.4 down, with their labels 19 to the left of each; a yellow section ring and screw between them. At the left, a 12.9 round point centred (10.2, 16.7) with the earth symbol under it (gaps: ground-point), and screws 6.2 from the left end at 7.2 and 36.6 down. The panel is symmetrical on the right, screws at 437.1.

input.note: drawing - INPUT "NEMA L5-30 PLUG", "10FT 10AWG / 3C POWERCORD"; INPUT RATING "100-127V~", "W+N+PE", "24A", "50/60HZ". The cord is fixed. The exporter writes a L5-30P cord as `other` with a label, as it does the cord of the PDUMV30, so `input-plug` is `other`.

method.note: FIGURES FROM THE MAKER'S SPECIFICATION DRAWING, MEASURED, NOT DIMENSIONED. Eaton EMIT03-10 ("ePDU G3 SPECIFICATION DRAWING FOR EMIT03-10", part EMI3MGB5EMB13A1, revision 002, 21 Jan 2016, one D-size sheet) is a vector sheet that dimensions only the overall: 482.6 [19.00] wide, 42.9 [1.69] high and 203.2 [8.00] deep. Every other figure was read off a 300 dpi render against the 482.6, 9.45 px per mm (the 42.9 and the 203.2 read 42.8 and 203.3 at that scale), good to about 0.5 mm. The sheet says "DO NOT SCALE DRAWING" and prints its own scale as 0.500 though it is drawn at about 0.8; the overall is the only scale used. The sheet gives four views: the face with the controls (below the plan), the plan (the top), the face with the cord (above the plan, turned half a turn, its labels upside down) and a pictorial at a third of the scale. THE REAR VIEW IS TURNED HALF A TURN ON THE SHEET and is drawn here as it stands, seen from behind. No photograph of this model is held. The brochure (Rack PDU G3+, BR155022EN, 2019, EMEA) has two small photographs of 1U horizontal G3+ units on its page 3 (their model numbers are not printed) and larger ones of vertical units on page 2; they show the meter module, the buttons, the display and the section colours, and are the colour reference here, not photographs of this model.

module.note: drawing and datasheet - the meter module is drawn as one plate with its ports, display and buttons. The Eaton Rack PDU G3 product overview (PA155003EN) says "Hot-swappable meter eliminates power disruption to your IT equipment when removing the meter" and the brochure shows the module out of the strip. IT IS NOT MODELLED AS A BAY: no held document dimensions the module apart from its faceplate or gives its depth (gaps: meter-module-bay), so its parts stand on the face. THE MODULE'S PORTS ARE NAMED BY THE G3 QUICK START (P-164000314_2, July 2014, page 2 table), not by this sheet: a serial or environmental probe (EMP) RJ-45 port (1), an Ethernet 10/100 Base-T port (4), a reset button (7) "insert a probe and press the button for 3 seconds", a USB port "used for firmware upgrade" (8) and a daisy chain port (9). The sheet draws three RJ-45 sockets and a USB-A socket: the one with the network symbol beside it is the Ethernet port, the stacked pair at the left is the serial and the daisy-chain port, and WHICH OF THE PAIR IS WHICH IS NOT STATED by any held figure (the quick start's module drawing is too small to read). The upper one is taken as the serial port, the lower one, under the chain symbol, as the daisy chain (gaps: module-port-order). The "R" and ring beside the USB port is the reset button.

outlets.note: drawing - "OUTPUT (12) NEMA 5-20R", OUTPUT RATING "100-127V~; 16A MAX PER OUTLET; 16A MAX PER SECTION; 24A MAX TOTAL". Numbered as printed, A1 and A2 on the controls face, A3 to A6 and B1 to B6 on the cord face. Each is drawn with its T neutral slot up, its earth hole to the left and its line slot down, as the sheet draws it (viewed from the face). The sheet's one-line diagram feeds section A and section B each through its own breaker (a metering point before it), so outlets A1 to A6 are `through: breaker-a` and B1 to B6 `through: breaker-b`.

rear.note: drawing - the cord face, seen from behind, so x runs the other way from the front: mm from the left as seen from behind. The cord gland, a hex nut 32.8 across flats and 37.9 across corners, centred 31.5 across; then A3 to A6 and B1 to B6, each 27 square, centred 72.8, 111.6, 148.4, 187.5, 224.3, 263.4, 300.2, 339.3, 376.1 and 415.1 across, all at 21.4 down. A section's two outlets sit about 39.1 apart with a ring and a screw between them (yellow for A, blue for B, at 92.0, 168.1, 243.9, 319.8 and 395.5), and neighbouring sections 36.8 apart. The labels A3 to B6 are printed beside each outlet. Screws stand 6.2 from each end at 7.2 and 36.2 down. THE DRAWN OUTLET OUTLINES ARE ABOUT 32 ACROSS, wider than the 27 face std/nema-5-20r@1 takes from the receptacle it follows; the part is placed on the drawn centre and its edge differs from the drawn one by about 2.5 on each side.
